title: Bajre ki Roti with Ghee & Jaggery
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (bajra flour, water, salt, ghee, jaggery). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.

ingredients.name: White butter (nooni ghee) or desi ghee, jaggery

recipe: Mix bajra flour with salt and hot water to form a soft, pliable dough. Knead well.
Pat into thick rotis by hand and cook on a hot tawa, pressing gently, till done on both sides.
Serve hot, smeared generously with white butter or ghee, and with jaggery on the side.
tips: Winter staple of Haryana – warming, rustic and deeply satisfying.
Hand-patted rotis have the best texture.

title: Besan Masala Roti
jainNotes: Contains green chilli and spices - no onion or garlic. Spice source verification recommended for strict Jain.

ingredients.name: Ajwain, amchur, green chilli, coriander, salt, ghee

recipe: Mix wheat flour and besan with ajwain, amchur, chopped green chilli, coriander, salt and a little ghee. Knead into a soft dough.
Roll into rotis and cook on a tawa with ghee till golden spots appear.
Serve hot with curd, raita or pickle.
tips: Flavourful gram-flour flatbread – a complete meal with curd.
Amchur gives the characteristic tang.

title: Bajra Khichdi with Moong Dal
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.

ingredients.name: Ghee, cumin, green chilli, ginger, salt

recipe: Wash and soak bajra and moong dal briefly. Cook together with water or buttermilk, salt and turmeric till soft and porridge-like.
Temper cumin, green chilli and ginger in ghee and pour over the khichdi.
Serve hot with extra ghee, curd or pickle.
tips: Hearty winter breakfast or meal – warming and nutritious.
Traditionally pounded bajra is preferred.

title: Bajra Khichdi with Mixed Dal
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.

ingredients.name: Ghee, cumin, green chilli, ginger, salt

recipe: Wash and soak bajra and mixed dal briefly. Cook together with water or buttermilk, salt and turmeric till soft and porridge-like.
Temper cumin, green chilli and ginger in ghee and pour over the khichdi.
Serve hot with extra ghee, curd or pickle.
tips: Hearty winter breakfast or meal made with mixed lentils.
Warming and nutritious.

title: Kadhi Pakora with Onion Pakoras
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, use spinach or plain pakoras.

ingredients.name: Cumin, fenugreek, dry red chilli, turmeric, salt

recipe: Whisk yogurt with besan and water. Cook slowly with turmeric and salt till it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Make soft onion pakoras, fry and add to the kadhi. Simmer.
Temper with cumin, fenugreek and dry red chilli in ghee. Serve with rice or bajra roti.
tips: Staple Haryanvi comfort food – tangy, filling and perfect with rice or millet roti.
Slightly sour yogurt gives the best flavour.

title: Kadhi Pakora with Spinach Pakoras
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.

ingredients.name: Besan, spinach, ginger, green chilli, spices for pakoras
Cumin, fenugreek, dry red chilli, turmeric, salt

recipe: Whisk yogurt with besan and water. Cook slowly with turmeric and salt till it thickens and the raw smell disappears.
Make soft spinach pakoras, fry and add to the kadhi. Simmer.
Temper with cumin, fenugreek and dry red chilli in ghee. Serve with rice or bajra roti.
tips: Staple Haryanvi comfort food with spinach pakoras - a healthier twist.
Tangy, filling and perfect with rice or millet roti.

title: Bathua Raita
jainNotes: Contains green chilli - no onion or garlic. Spice source verification recommended for strict Jain.

ingredients.name: Roasted cumin, black salt, green chilli (optional)

recipe: Wash and boil or steam bathua leaves till soft. Squeeze out excess water and chop finely.
Mix into beaten curd with roasted cumin powder, black salt and optional green chilli.
Serve chilled as a cooling side with roti, khichdi or any meal.
tips: Seasonal winter raita – nutritious and cooling despite the season.
Bathua is a classic Haryanvi green.

title: Mixed Dal
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.

ingredients.name: Ghee, cumin, turmeric, garam masala, salt

recipe: Pressure-cook the mixed dals with turmeric and salt till soft. Mash lightly.
Prepare a tempering of ghee, cumin, onion, ginger-garlic and tomato. Add to the dal and simmer.
Finish with garam masala. Serve with roti or rice.
tips: Everyday protein-rich dal of Haryanvi homes – slow-cooked with generous ghee.
The mix of lentils gives depth.

title: Singri ki Sabzi
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.
recipe: Soak dried singri. Cook with spices and yogurt-based gravy until soft and well-flavoured.
Serve with bajra or wheat roti.
tips: Rustic sabzi with Rajasthani-Haryanvi desert influence.
The dried beans have a unique texture and taste.

title: Hara Dhania Cholia
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
recipe: Sauté cumin, ginger and green chilli. Add the green chickpeas and cook till tender.
Finish with a generous amount of fresh coriander.
Serve with roti or as a seasonal side.
tips: Seasonal winter delicacy – fresh green chickpeas with lots of coriander.
Simple and full of local flavour.

title: Churma
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (wheat flour, ghee, jaggery, cardamom). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Make a stiff dough with wheat flour and ghee. Form into balls or thick rotis and cook on a tawa or deep-fry till fully cooked and crisp.
Crush into coarse crumbs. Mix with melted jaggery or bura and more ghee. Add cardamom and nuts if desired.
Serve as a sweet side or snack.
tips: Classic Haryanvi sweet made from crushed wheat – often eaten with dal or as part of a thali.
Generous ghee is traditional.

title: Atta Pinni
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (wheat flour, ghee, jaggery, nuts). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Roast the wheat flour in ghee till aromatic and golden. Add crushed nuts.
Mix with melted jaggery or bura while warm. Shape into small laddus or pinnis while still warm.
Store in an airtight container. A winter energy sweet.
tips: Traditional winter sweet of Haryana – dense, rich and nourishing.
Made with wheat flour.

title: Alsi Pinni (Flaxseed Pinni)
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (flaxseed, wheat flour, ghee, jaggery). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
recipe: Roast the flour mixture with flaxseed in ghee till aromatic and golden. Add crushed nuts.
Mix with melted jaggery or bura while warm. Shape into small laddus or pinnis while still warm.
Store in an airtight container. A winter energy sweet.
tips: Traditional winter sweet of Haryana – dense, rich and nourishing.
Alsi pinni is especially valued for its warming properties and omega-3 content.

title: Kachri ki Sabzi (with Dried Kachri)
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.
recipe: Soak dried kachri. Sauté onion and spices, then add kachri and cook till soft and well-spiced.
Serve with bajra or wheat roti.
tips: Tangy sabzi made from the local wild cucumber – unique to the region.
Pairs especially well with millet rotis.

title: Methi Gajar
jainNotes: Contains carrot (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains.

ingredients.name: Cumin, green chilli, oil or ghee, salt

recipe: Chop methi and carrot. Heat oil/ghee, add cumin and green chilli.
Add carrot and cook till almost done, then add methi and salt. Stir-fry till the greens wilt and flavours blend.
Serve with roti or bajra roti.
tips: Seasonal winter sabzi – simple, slightly bitter-sweet and very Haryanvi.
Minimal spices highlight the vegetables.
